question.text: Why do special laws apply to every North Carolina driver under eighteen?

answer.text: Every driver under eighteen is a provisional licensee, and special laws apply because this group has a much higher crash rate.

teaching.text: Drivers under eighteen have a much higher crash rate, so every one of them is a provisional licensee under special laws. Remember: under eighteen means provisional.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every driver under eighteen is a provisional licensee, and special laws apply because this group has a much higher crash rate.

question.text: Who may hold a Level One Limited Learner Permit?

answer.text: The Level One Limited Learner Permit is for North Carolina residents at least fifteen but under eighteen who will drive vehicles needing a Class C license.

teaching.text: Level One is for North Carolina residents from fifteen up to eighteen who will drive Class C vehicles. Remember: fifteen to seventeen, Class C.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Level One Limited Learner Permit is for North Carolina residents at least fifteen but under eighteen who will drive vehicles needing a Class C license.

question.text: What certificate must a teen show before taking the permit test?

answer.text: Before taking the permit test, a teen must show a certificate for an approved driver education course with at least thirty hours in the classroom and six hours behind the wheel.

teaching.text: The approved course certificate shows at least thirty classroom hours and six hours behind the wheel. Remember: classroom plus behind the wheel.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before taking the permit test, a teen must show a certificate for an approved driver education course with at least thirty hours in the classroom and six hours behind the wheel.

question.text: Before testing for a permit or a license, what must a driver under eighteen show?

answer.text: A driver under eighteen must show the driver education certificate, at least thirty classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours, before testing for either a learner permit or a license.

teaching.text: Any driver under eighteen shows the driver education certificate before testing for a permit or a license. Remember: certificate before any test.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver under eighteen must show the driver education certificate, at least thirty classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours, before testing for either a learner permit or a license.

question.text: Which tests must a Level One applicant pass?

answer.text: A Level One applicant must pass the written, sign and vision tests.

teaching.text: The Level One applicant passes the written test, the sign test and the vision test. Remember: written, sign, vision.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Level One applicant must pass the written, sign and vision tests.

question.text: Whose signature does a minor need for a permit or license?

answer.text: A parent or legal guardian must sign for a minor's permit or license.

teaching.text: Because the applicant is a minor, a parent or legal guardian signs for the permit or license. Remember: a parent signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A parent or legal guardian must sign for a minor's permit or license.

question.text: Who may serve as a Level One supervising driver?

answer.text: A supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent or guardian, or a responsible adult the parent or guardian approves, and must hold a valid license that has been held for at least five years.

teaching.text: The supervisor is a parent, grandparent, guardian or approved adult whose valid license has been held at least five years. Remember: family adult, licensed five years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent or guardian, or a responsible adult the parent or guardian approves, and must hold a valid license that has been held for at least five years.

question.text: During the first six months of Level One, when and how may the teen drive?

answer.text: For the first six months, a Level One permit holder may drive only from five a.m. to nine p.m., and only with the supervising driver.

teaching.text: For the first six months, drive only from five in the morning to nine at night, and only with the supervising driver. Remember: five to nine, supervised.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For the first six months, a Level One permit holder may drive only from five a.m. to nine p.m., and only with the supervising driver.

question.text: What changes for a Level One holder after six months?

answer.text: Once six months have passed since Level One was issued, the holder may drive at any hour, still with a supervising driver.

teaching.text: After six months the hours open to any time of day, but the supervising driver still rides along. Remember: any hour, still supervised.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once six months have passed since Level One was issued, the holder may drive at any hour, still with a supervising driver.

question.text: How do the two Level One time phases differ, and what stays the same?

answer.text: Level One has two time phases: in the first six months driving is limited to five a.m. to nine p.m., and after that any hour is allowed, but a supervising driver is required in both phases.

teaching.text: The second phase widens the clock, but a supervising driver is required in both Level One phases. Remember: hours open, supervisor stays.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Level One has two time phases: in the first six months driving is limited to five a.m. to nine p.m., and after that any hour is allowed, but a supervising driver is required in both phases.

question.text: At Level One, who must buckle up and who may sit in front?

answer.text: With a Level One permit, every passenger must wear a seat belt or ride in a child safety seat, and only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

teaching.text: Every passenger is belted or in a child safety seat, and only the driver and supervisor sit in front. Remember: front seat for two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With a Level One permit, every passenger must wear a seat belt or ride in a child safety seat, and only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

question.text: Which level has the rule that only the driver and supervising driver sit in front?

answer.text: The front-seat rule belongs to Level One: only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

teaching.text: The rule reserving the front seat for the driver and supervisor belongs to Level One. Remember: front-seat rule is Level One.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The front-seat rule belongs to Level One: only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

question.text: May a Level One driver use a cell phone or connected phone technology while driving?

answer.text: A Level One driver may not use a cell phone or any connected cell-phone technology while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

teaching.text: No cell phone and no connected phone technology while driving on public roads at Level One. Remember: no phone at Level One.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Level One driver may not use a cell phone or any connected cell-phone technology while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

question.text: Which calls are the only cell phone exception for a teen driver?

answer.text: The only cell phone exception for a teen driver is an emergency call to an emergency operator, a hospital, doctor's office or clinic, an ambulance service, a fire department, a law enforcement agency, or a parent, legal guardian or spouse.

teaching.text: The only allowed calls are emergency calls to emergency services, medical providers, law enforcement, or a parent, guardian or spouse. Remember: emergency calls only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The only cell phone exception for a teen driver is an emergency call to an emergency operator, a hospital, doctor's office or clinic, an ambulance service, a fire department, a law enforcement agency, or a parent, legal guardian or spouse.

question.text: How long must a teen keep the Level One permit before applying for Level Two?

answer.text: A teen must keep the Level One permit for nine months before applying for the Limited Provisional License.

teaching.text: The Level One permit is held for nine months before the Level Two application. Remember: nine months at Level One.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A teen must keep the Level One permit for nine months before applying for the Limited Provisional License.

question.text: How many hours must the Level One driving log record, and how many at night?

answer.text: The Level One driving log must record at least sixty hours behind the wheel, with at least ten of those hours at night.

teaching.text: The log needs at least sixty hours behind the wheel, and at least ten of them at night. Remember: sixty logged, ten dark.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Level One driving log must record at least sixty hours behind the wheel, with at least ten of those hours at night.

question.text: For the driving log, what counts as daytime driving and what counts as night driving?

answer.text: For the log, daytime driving means sunrise to sunset while there is daylight, and night driving means after sunset when there is no daylight.

teaching.text: Daytime is sunrise to sunset with daylight, and night is after sunset with no daylight. Remember: daylight is day, dark is night.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For the log, daytime driving means sunrise to sunset while there is daylight, and night driving means after sunset when there is no daylight.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: daylight is day, dark is night

question.text: Who signs the driving log, and when is it turned in?

answer.text: The supervising driver signs the driving log, and it is turned in to the Division when the teen applies for the Limited Provisional License.

teaching.text: The supervising driver signs the log, and it goes to the Division with the Level Two application. Remember: supervisor signs, hand it in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The supervising driver signs the driving log, and it is turned in to the Division when the teen applies for the Limited Provisional License.

question.text: How is the Level One holding period different from the driving log requirement?

answer.text: The Level One holding period is nine months, while the driving log needs at least sixty hours with ten at night; these are different requirements that both apply before Level Two.

teaching.text: The nine months and the sixty logged hours are separate requirements, and both must be met. Remember: months held, hours logged.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Level One holding period is nine months, while the driving log needs at least sixty hours with ten at night; these are different requirements that both apply before Level Two.

question.text: What record must a teen have before moving up to Level Two?

answer.text: To move up to Level Two, the teen must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions during the previous six months.

teaching.text: No moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions in the six months before moving up to Level Two. Remember: six clean months.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To move up to Level Two, the teen must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions during the previous six months.

question.text: Who may hold a Level Two Limited Provisional License?

answer.text: The Level Two Limited Provisional License is for drivers at least sixteen but under eighteen.

teaching.text: Level Two is for drivers at least sixteen but under eighteen. Remember: sixteen to seventeen.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Level Two Limited Provisional License is for drivers at least sixteen but under eighteen.

question.text: When may a Level Two driver drive alone?

answer.text: A Level Two driver may drive alone from five a.m. to nine p.m., and at any hour when going straight to or from work or a volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service they belong to.

teaching.text: Drive alone from five in the morning to nine at night, or at any hour going straight to or from work or volunteer emergency service. Remember: five to nine, or duty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Level Two driver may drive alone from five a.m. to nine p.m., and at any hour when going straight to or from work or a volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service they belong to.

question.text: Which level is the first that allows driving without a supervisor?

answer.text: Level Two is the first level that allows driving alone, and only from five a.m. to nine p.m. or when going straight to or from work or a volunteer emergency service.

teaching.text: Level One never allows driving alone, so Level Two is the first solo level. Remember: Level Two goes solo.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Level Two is the first level that allows driving alone, and only from five a.m. to nine p.m. or when going straight to or from work or a volunteer emergency service.

question.text: At Level Two, who must buckle up, and where does a required supervisor sit?

answer.text: At Level Two, all passengers must be belted or in a child safety seat, and when supervision is required the supervising driver sits beside the driver.

teaching.text: All passengers are belted, and when supervision is required the supervisor sits beside the driver. Remember: everyone belted, supervisor beside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At Level Two, all passengers must be belted or in a child safety seat, and when supervision is required the supervising driver sits beside the driver.

question.text: Driving unsupervised at Level Two, how many under-twenty-one passengers from outside the household may ride along?

answer.text: Driving unsupervised at Level Two, a teen may carry only one passenger under twenty-one who does not live in the same household.

teaching.text: Unsupervised, carry only one passenger under twenty-one who lives outside your household. Remember: one outside rider.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving unsupervised at Level Two, a teen may carry only one passenger under twenty-one who does not live in the same household.

question.text: When may a Level Two driver carry one more under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household?

answer.text: One additional under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household is allowed only when that passenger is a student being driven directly to or from school.

teaching.text: A second outside passenger under twenty-one is allowed only for a student riding directly to or from school. Remember: extra rider is a student.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: One additional under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household is allowed only when that passenger is a student being driven directly to or from school.

question.text: What is the under-twenty-one passenger rule when every passenger lives in the driver's household?

answer.text: If every passenger lives in the driver's household there is no under-twenty-one limit, but under-twenty-one household members may not ride along while under-twenty-one non-household passengers are aboard.

teaching.text: Household-only groups have no under-twenty-one limit, but household teens may not ride with outside teens. Remember: household riders, no limit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If every passenger lives in the driver's household there is no under-twenty-one limit, but under-twenty-one household members may not ride along while under-twenty-one non-household passengers are aboard.

question.text: Which passengers does the Level Two limit actually count?

answer.text: The Level Two passenger limit counts under-twenty-one passengers from outside the household when driving unsupervised; household members alone have no limit, except they cannot ride with under-twenty-one non-household passengers.

teaching.text: The limit counts young riders from outside the household, and household members may not be mixed in with them. Remember: count outsiders under twenty-one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Level Two passenger limit counts under-twenty-one passengers from outside the household when driving unsupervised; household members alone have no limit, except they cannot ride with under-twenty-one non-household passengers.

question.text: Does the cell phone ban continue at Level Two?

answer.text: Level Two drivers face the same cell phone ban and the same short list of emergency-call exceptions as Level One drivers.

teaching.text: The same phone ban and the same emergency-call exceptions carry over from Level One. Remember: same ban, same exceptions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Level Two drivers face the same cell phone ban and the same short list of emergency-call exceptions as Level One drivers.

question.text: How long must a teen hold Level Two before applying for the Full Provisional License?

answer.text: A teen must hold the Level Two license for at least six months before applying for the Full Provisional License.

teaching.text: Level Two is held for at least six months before applying for the Full Provisional License. Remember: six months at Level Two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A teen must hold the Level Two license for at least six months before applying for the Full Provisional License.

question.text: Which holding period is shorter, Level One or Level Two?

answer.text: Level Two must be held for at least six months before the Full Provisional License, which is shorter than the nine-month Level One holding period.

teaching.text: Level One is held nine months, then Level Two at least six, so the second hold is shorter. Remember: nine first, then six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Level Two must be held for at least six months before the Full Provisional License, which is shorter than the nine-month Level One holding period.

question.text: What record must a driver have before moving up to Level Three?

answer.text: To move up to Level Three, the driver must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions in the previous six months.

teaching.text: Six months with no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions comes before Level Three. Remember: six clean months again.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To move up to Level Three, the driver must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions in the previous six months.

question.text: How can an eligible driver upgrade to Level Three or to a regular Class C at eighteen?

answer.text: An eligible driver can upgrade from Level Two to the Level Three Full Provisional License online, and can upgrade to a regular Class C license online at age eighteen.

teaching.text: An eligible driver upgrades online to Level Three, and online again to a regular Class C at eighteen. Remember: upgrade online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An eligible driver can upgrade from Level Two to the Level Three Full Provisional License online, and can upgrade to a regular Class C license online at age eighteen.

question.text: Which limits does a Full Provisional License drop?

answer.text: A Full Provisional License drops the Level One and Level Two limits on driving hours, supervision and passengers.

teaching.text: The Full Provisional License lifts the hour, supervision and passenger limits of the earlier levels. Remember: hours, supervisor, passengers lifted.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Full Provisional License drops the Level One and Level Two limits on driving hours, supervision and passengers.

question.text: May a Full Provisional licensee under eighteen use a cell phone while driving?

answer.text: A Full Provisional licensee who is still under eighteen may not use a cell phone while driving, apart from the same emergency calls.

teaching.text: Under eighteen, a full provisional driver still may not use a cell phone except for the emergency calls. Remember: still no phone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Full Provisional licensee who is still under eighteen may not use a cell phone while driving, apart from the same emergency calls.

question.text: Which rule still applies after the Full Provisional License lifts the other limits?

answer.text: The Full Provisional License lifts the hour, supervision and passenger limits, yet a driver under eighteen still may not use a cell phone except for listed emergency calls.

teaching.text: Hours, supervision and passenger limits are lifted, but the phone ban stays until eighteen. Remember: lifted limits, phone ban stays.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Full Provisional License lifts the hour, supervision and passenger limits, yet a driver under eighteen still may not use a cell phone except for listed emergency calls.

question.text: What should a new resident aged fifteen to seventeen with an out-of-state permit or license do?

answer.text: A new North Carolina resident aged fifteen to seventeen who holds a permit or license from elsewhere should contact a local driver license office to learn which permit or license they qualify for.

teaching.text: A teen moving in with a permit or license from elsewhere contacts a local driver license office to learn what applies. Remember: call the local office.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A new North Carolina resident aged fifteen to seventeen who holds a permit or license from elsewhere should contact a local driver license office to learn which permit or license they qualify for.

question.text: How does the DMV treat a provisional licensee's driving record?

answer.text: The DMV watches a provisional licensee's driving record more closely and may contact the driver after certain convictions or crashes.

teaching.text: The DMV watches a young driver's record closely and may reach out after certain convictions or crashes. Remember: record watched closely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The DMV watches a provisional licensee's driving record more closely and may contact the driver after certain convictions or crashes.

question.text: What is the alcohol and drug rule for a provisional licensee, and the penalty?

answer.text: A provisional licensee may not drive after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs, and a conviction brings a one-year license revocation.

teaching.text: A provisional licensee may not drive after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs, and a conviction means a one-year revocation. Remember: not one drop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A provisional licensee may not drive after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs, and a conviction brings a one-year license revocation.

question.text: Is the provisional alcohol rule a blood alcohol limit?

answer.text: For a provisional licensee the alcohol rule is any amount, not a blood alcohol limit, and a conviction means a one-year revocation.

teaching.text: The teen rule is any amount at all, not a blood alcohol limit. Remember: any amount, not a limit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a provisional licensee the alcohol rule is any amount, not a blood alcohol limit, and a conviction means a one-year revocation.

question.text: Which phone activities are banned for a provisional licensee while driving?

answer.text: A provisional licensee may not use a cellphone, type multiple letters or text to communicate, or read email or text messages while driving.

teaching.text: No phone calls, no typing or texting, and no reading email or texts while driving. Remember: no calls, texts or email.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A provisional licensee may not use a cellphone, type multiple letters or text to communicate, or read email or text messages while driving.

question.text: Who must wear a seat belt in a vehicle driven by a provisional licensee?

answer.text: Everyone riding in a moving vehicle driven by a provisional licensee must have a seat belt properly fastened.

teaching.text: Every rider in a car driven by a provisional licensee wears a properly fastened seat belt. Remember: everyone buckles up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Everyone riding in a moving vehicle driven by a provisional licensee must have a seat belt properly fastened.

question.text: What school discipline can cost a student the license, and for how long?

answer.text: A student loses their license if suspended from school for more than ten days in a row, or sent to an alternative educational setting for discipline for more than ten days in a row, and the loss lasts twelve months.

teaching.text: More than ten school days in a row of suspension or disciplinary placement costs the license for twelve months. Remember: lose control, lose your license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A student loses their license if suspended from school for more than ten days in a row, or sent to an alternative educational setting for discipline for more than ten days in a row, and the loss lasts twelve months.

question.text: Is the Lose Control, Lose Your License rule about traffic violations?

answer.text: Lose Control, Lose Your License is about school discipline, more than ten consecutive days of suspension or alternative placement, not about traffic violations.

teaching.text: This rule is triggered by school discipline, not by traffic tickets. Remember: school discipline, not traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lose Control, Lose Your License is about school discipline, more than ten consecutive days of suspension or alternative placement, not about traffic violations.

question.text: What kinds of safety restrictions can be placed on a license?

answer.text: A license can be restricted for safety, for example to driving only while wearing corrective lenses or only with equipment needed to drive safely.

teaching.text: A license can require corrective lenses or the equipment a driver needs to drive safely. Remember: lenses or equipment required.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license can be restricted for safety, for example to driving only while wearing corrective lenses or only with equipment needed to drive safely.

question.text: How is a driver treated after going outside a license restriction?

answer.text: A driver who goes outside the limits of a license restriction is treated as driving without a license.

teaching.text: Driving outside a restriction is treated the same as driving without a license. Remember: outside the limit, unlicensed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver who goes outside the limits of a license restriction is treated as driving without a license.

question.text: Is breaking a license restriction a minor infraction?

answer.text: A license restriction is a limit you must stay within; breaking it is not a minor infraction but counts as driving without a license.

teaching.text: A restriction is binding, so breaking it is not a minor infraction. Remember: restrictions are binding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license restriction is a limit you must stay within; breaking it is not a minor infraction but counts as driving without a license.

question.text: What may the DMV do with the documents you bring?

answer.text: The DMV may copy your documents or hold them briefly to check that they are genuine, and it rejects any document that shows alteration.

teaching.text: Documents may be copied or held briefly to check them, and any altered document is rejected. Remember: copied, checked, altered rejected.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The DMV may copy your documents or hold them briefly to check that they are genuine, and it rejects any document that shows alteration.

question.text: What must a first-time North Carolina applicant prove?

answer.text: A first-time North Carolina applicant must prove full name and date of birth, North Carolina residence address, and a Social Security number or legal presence in the U.S.

teaching.text: Prove your full name and birth date, your North Carolina address, and a Social Security number or legal presence. Remember: name, birth, address, status.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A first-time North Carolina applicant must prove full name and date of birth, North Carolina residence address, and a Social Security number or legal presence in the U.S.

question.text: What insurance proof must a driver license applicant show?

answer.text: Applicants for a driver license must also show proof of vehicle liability insurance.

teaching.text: License applicants also show proof of vehicle liability insurance. Remember: show liability insurance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants for a driver license must also show proof of vehicle liability insurance.

question.text: Is a card marked Not for Federal Identification still valid in North Carolina?

answer.text: A North Carolina card marked Not for Federal Identification is still a valid state license, permit or ID.

teaching.text: The Not for Federal Identification marking does not stop the card from being a valid state license, permit or ID. Remember: still valid in state.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A North Carolina card marked Not for Federal Identification is still a valid state license, permit or ID.

question.text: What do Not for Federal Identification card holders need for flights or federal facilities?

answer.text: Beginning May seven, two thousand twenty-five, holders of a Not for Federal Identification card need extra documents to board commercial flights or enter federal facilities, military bases or nuclear power plants that require identification.

teaching.text: From May seventh, two thousand twenty-five, flights and federal facilities need extra documents with that card. Remember: federal uses need more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Beginning May seven, two thousand twenty-five, holders of a Not for Federal Identification card need extra documents to board commercial flights or enter federal facilities, military bases or nuclear power plants that require identification.
